Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 3. Aluminum hydroxide also decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, and this interaction is specific to their oral forms. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug, separating administration by at least 2 hours, and monitoring closely. 4. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of tiludronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and administration should be separated by 2 hours with close monitoring. 5. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of timolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is recommended, with administration separated by 2 hours and close monitoring. 6. Tobramycin reduces magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 7. Torsemide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. This interaction is also minor, with unknown clinical significance. 8. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of trandolapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 9. Triamterene increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 10. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of ursodiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 11. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, which reduces bioavailability. The impact on efficacy is unknown. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 12. Aluminum hydroxide similarly decreases the levels or effects of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, reducing bioavailability. The effect on efficacy remains unknown. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 13. Vitamin D increases magnesium hydroxide levels by raising serum magnesium concentrations, particularly in patients with renal impairment. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 14. Vitamin D also increases aluminum hydroxide levels, and coadministration should be avoided. Chronic use of aluminum-containing antacids with vitamin D can lead to aluminum retention and potential toxicity. 15. Aluminum hydroxide interacts with willow bark through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 16. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses but decrease at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. 17. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of zoledronic acid by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, with administration separated by 2 hours and close monitoring. 18. Hypersensitivity to any component of the formulation should be considered. 19. Caution is advised in patients with renal failure. 20. Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide may alter the rate or extent of absorption of concomitantly administered oral drugs by changing gastrointestinal transit time or binding the drug. 21. Patients on magnesium-restricted diets should exercise caution. 22. Similar trade names may have different compositions, so careful review is necessary. 23. Combination products containing aluminum hydroxide or magnesium hydroxide should not be used for hyperphosphatemia. 24. Pregnancy Category C: The safety of these agents during pregnancy is not well established. 25. Lactation: Excretion of these agents in breast milk is unknown. 26. Pregnancy Category A: Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk.
